messages.subject: rstanarm -- stan_polr -- log-fit_ratio -- model fit
parts:
Background: In the stan_lm example provided on this page, the authors refer to log-fit_ratio as a determinate of whether the model over or under-fits the data. 

Problem/question: I created a different model using stan_polr and I cannot seem to find log-fit_ratio. Shouldn't the output for stan_polr also provide log-fit_ratio?

Below is my code:
R2prior <- R2(location = 0.12 , what = "mode")
mod <- Ordinal ~ zAge + English_proficiency + Education + zShipley_vocabulary + zSAHLE + zWM_proportion_correct + zSpoonerisms_total + zMEDCO + zFlesch + zRDL2
post <- stan_polr(formula = mod , data = Study3 , prior = R2prior)
print (post)

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstanarm -- stan_polr -- log-fit_ratio -- model fit
parts:
On Monday, April 17, 2017 at 12:28:00 PM UTC-4, Michael Ratajczak wrote:
Background: In the stan_lm example provided on this page, the authors refer to log-fit_ratio as a determinate of whether the model over or under-fits the data. 

Problem/question: I created a different model using stan_polr and I cannot seem to find log-fit_ratio. Shouldn't the output for stan_polr also provide log-fit_ratio?
No. The stan_lm() function estimates the error variance, whereas the stan_polr() function does not (it is fixed to 1).
